title: A failed Clerk user sync left no ERROR row in the integration audit log: the row was written on the transaction the failure had aborted
short: Failure audit lost in aborted tx
summary: On 2026-11-19 at 06:43Z, on dev, a Clerk `user.created` event carried an email that another product user (other external id) already held. The upsert failed on `product_users_product_id_email_key` (23505) on all 6 attempts, and each time the handler's `UPSERT_USER` ERROR audit row failed with 25P02, because it was written on the command transaction the failed insert had just aborted. This is root cause R4 of the [2026-10-07 postmortem](2026-10-07-duplicate-clerk-reconcile.md): its action A4 (anchor#210) stayed open for 43 days while the ledger row was marked verified. The fix lets a command handler return its failure audit row with the error, and the webhook and reconcile paths write it in a fresh transaction after the rollback; a ruleguard rule refuses the old pattern. The email conflict itself comes from Clerk events applied without ordering, a design change deferred by anchor#399.

impact.text: Dev only, no customer impact. One Clerk event failed permanently after 6 attempts, and the integration audit log lost the 6 `UPSERT_USER` ERROR rows that name the failing external id; the phase-2 retry and failure rows were kept. Prod runs the same code: any Clerk upsert or delete failure there lost its row too, and a failed reconcile batch left no failure row at all.

numbers.label: the A4 fix for this class stayed open

trigger: A Clerk `user.created` event for product `prd_3MJZRxg3…` (MCP audit Clerk probes) whose email another external id already held; the upsert raised 23505 and aborted the command transaction.
detection: The grafana-watch routine found the paired `failed to upsert product user` / `failed to create integration audit log … (25P02)` rows in its 2026-11-19T09:02Z scan, about 2 h 18 min later, and recorded ledger row 102. Detection was good enough for a dev-only loss: since the fix, a failed command leaves an ERROR row a product owner sees in the audit log.
resolution: The impact ended when the event exhausted its retries at 06:44:12Z. The fix (this PR) adds `provider.WithFailureAudit`: the Clerk upsert and delete handlers return their ERROR audit row with the error, `handleEventFailure` writes it in the phase-2 transaction, and `executeCommandsInBatches` writes it in a new transaction after a reconcile batch rolls back. A ruleguard rule reports any `provider.WriteAuditLog` of an ERROR row, and a component test asserts the row after a forced 23505.

whys.problem: A failed Clerk user sync left no UPSERT_USER ERROR row in the integration audit log

because.text: The handler's audit insert failed with 25P02: current transaction is aborted
because.evidence: 6 pairs of `failed to upsert product user` + `failed to create integration audit log … (25P02)`, 2026-11-19 06:43:54–06:44:12Z (VictoriaLogs, dev anchor)

because.text: The audit row was written on the caller's context, which joins the phase-1 command transaction the 23505 aborted
because.evidence: `executeUpsertUser` calls `provider.WriteAuditLog(ctx, …)` after `InTx` returns; `processOneEvent` runs it inside phase 1, `executeCommandsInBatches` inside the batch tx (`integration_service.go`)

because.text: WriteAuditLog accepts any context, and no test, type or lint told a handler that its failure row needs a transaction of its own
because.evidence: `internal/integration/provider/audit.go` on 61d4fcdd; no CT asserted a failure audit row

because.text: Command handlers record failures on the transaction that failed, with no guard against it
The upsert failed: the event's email was already held by a product user with another external id
because.evidence: `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "product_users_product_id_email_key" (23505)` on every attempt

because.text: Clerk events are applied in arrival order, and nothing decides what a stale row holding the same email means
because.evidence: anchor#399 audit finding `clerk-upsert-no-ordering-email-conflict`, deferred as design

because.text: The Clerk upsert has no event ordering and no rule for a stale product user that holds the email
The same loss had been found and named on 2026-10-07, so it should not have recurred
A4 stayed open 43 days past nothing: no run picked it up
because.evidence: anchor#210 open with no PR; status note 2026-11-16 'Still open'

because.text: The ledger row went verified when its log line stopped, and verified rows are not re-checked
because.evidence: ledger row 22: `verified (no 23505 from 2026-10-08T19:15…)` with A4 still open

because.text: A ledger row could reach verified while its postmortem still had open agent actions

contributing: The phase-2 retry rows carried the error text, so the audit log was not empty and the gap was easy to miss.
The reconcile path has no phase 2 at all: a failed batch left no failure row of any kind.

well: Every lost audit insert logged its own error with `code.file.path`, so the cause was one query away.
The 10-07 postmortem had already named the exact mechanism and the fix options.
wrong: An action tracked only in an issue was forgotten once its ledger row closed.
Two runs deferred row 102 for budget before anyone wrote its postmortem.
lucky: It happened on dev, from an audit probe. On prod a real customer's failed sync would have left no ERROR row in the log they read.
The 23505 was permanent and loud. A transient failure would have retried to success and hidden the lost row entirely.

actions.what: Return failure audit rows with the error (`provider.WithFailureAudit`); write them after the rollback in the webhook and reconcile paths; ruleguard `failureAuditLeavesTheAbortedTx`; CT `TestClerkWebhookFailedCommandAudit`
Postmortem loop: a ledger row reaches verified only when every action of its postmortem is done or owned by a human
Design change: order Clerk events per user and decide how a stale product user that holds the email is resolved

messaging.internal: Dev anchor: a failed Clerk user sync lost its UPSERT_USER ERROR audit row (25P02 on the aborted command tx), the R4 class from 2026-10-07. Fixed: failure audit rows now ride the error to a fresh transaction, with a lint rule and a CT. Clerk event ordering stays a design item.
